nodes.description: Private uint256 secret number (1-10) that players must guess.
Public timestamp of the last play, used in the kill time check.
Public bet price (0.001 ether) required to call play.
Public address of the contract owner, set from msg.sender in the constructor.
Public array of Game structs recording each play.
Constructor: sets ownerAddr to msg.sender and calls shuffle.
Internal function that pseudo-randomly sets secretNumber from block data.
Payable public function taking a guess, records the game and pays out the balance on a win.
Owner-only function that self-destructs the contract after a 6 hour delay.
Payable fallback function accepting plain ether transfers.
Caller-controlled address used for ownership, game recording and payouts.
Block timestamp (now) used for randomness and the kill time gate.
msg.sender.transfer(this.balance) sends the entire contract balance to the player.
suicide(msg.sender) destroys the contract and forwards the balance.
Arithmetic/time comparison now > lastPlayed + 6 hours gating the kill function.
sha3(now, block.blockhash(...)) used to derive secretNumber, predictable randomness.
Local Game struct instance built and pushed into gamesPlayed inside play().

edges.reason: msg.sender is assigned to ownerAddr in the constructor, establishing ownership from an untrusted caller.
msg.sender is written into the local Game struct field game.player.
The play() number parameter is stored into game.number of the local Game struct.
block.timestamp (now) feeds the sha3 call that produces the pseudo-random value.
The timestamp-derived randomness result is assigned to secretNumber in shuffle().
now is assigned to lastPlayed at the end of play(), a timestamp dependency.
lastPlayed is read as an operand of the now > lastPlayed + 6 hours comparison.
block.timestamp is compared against lastPlayed to gate kill(), a timestamp dependency.
The constructor invokes shuffle() to initialize secretNumber.
shuffle() writes the secretNumber state variable.
play() pushes the built Game struct into the gamesPlayed array.
play() reaches the external transfer of the whole contract balance when the guess is correct.
msg.sender is the recipient of the transfer, tying the payout to the untrusted caller.
play() updates the lastPlayed state variable.
play() reads secretNumber in the winning-guess comparison.
The number parameter is compared against secretNumber inside play().
kill() reaches suicide(msg.sender) which destroys the contract and sends the balance.
msg.sender is checked against ownerAddr to authorize kill().
ownerAddr is the privileged value that gates the kill() function.
kill() depends on the timestamp-based comparison before self-destructing.
kill() reads lastPlayed as part of its time-delay condition.
The external value transfer can invoke the recipient's fallback/receive code, enabling re-entry.

normalization_plan.reason: The number parameter is only used inside play() for the guess comparison and Game recording, so it should be folded into the play function node.
The local Game struct exists solely inside play() to be pushed into gamesPlayed, so it should be merged into the play function node.
